predecessors.name: Timurid Empire
predecessors.text: Samarkand, Bukhara, the Fergana towns, Khwarazm, Balkh and Herat, taken from the Timurids between 1500 and 1507

successors.name: Khanate of Bukhara
successors.text: the land between the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya, which Babur's defeat at Ghazdewan in 1512 'finally secured' for the Uzbeks

successors.name: Khanate of Khiva
successors.text: Khwarazm, where 'in 1511 his garrison was expelled and power passed to Ilbars'

successors.name: Safavid dynasty
successors.text: western Khorasan, Herat and Merv, conquered by Shah Ismail I in 1510

successors.name: Kazakh Khanate
successors.text: "all former Uzbek lands north of the Syr Darya" (Kasym Khan page), within Cliopatria's 1521 Kazakh shape

ledger.x: 1497: the Shaybanid holdings on the Syr Darya, the first Shaybanid shape in Cliopatria.
1500: Shaybani takes Samarkand from the Timurids.
1502: Fergana and Khujand pass to the Uzbeks.
1505: Shaybani takes Urgench after a ten-month siege and annexes Khwarazm.
1510: the Uzbeks give up the Syr Darya lands north of the river to Kasym.
2 December 1510: Muhammad Shaybani is killed at Merv.
December 1510: Khorasan, Herat and Merv pass to the Safavids after Merv; the Merv page also has Ismail expel the Uzbeks from Merv in 1510.
December 1510: Khwarazm passes to the Safavids after Merv.
1511: Babur takes Samarkand and Bukhara from the Uzbeks.
1511: the Shaybanid empire ends with Transoxiana left to the Uzbek khans of Bukhara and Samarkand, less the two cities Babur held in 1511 (the loss above).

wars.name: Shaybanid conquest of Transoxiana, Khwarazm and Khorasan
wars.outcome: Shaybani ousts the Timurids from Samarkand (1500), takes Bukhara (1501), Urgench (1505), Balkh (1506) and Herat (1507).

wars.name: Shaybanid-Safavid war and the Battle of Merv
wars.outcome: Ismail I invades Khorasan, besieges Merv for a month and defeats and kills Shaybani there (2 December 1510); the Safavids keep Khorasan.

wars.name: Shaybanid-Kazakh border raids
wars.outcome: Shaybani raided northwards in 1508-1509, 'pillaging the land of the Kazakh Khanate'; in 1510 Kasym Khan 'inflicted a major defeat on a large Uzbek force'.

certainty.note: A steppe and oasis empire: city holdings are known, frontiers between them are not surveyed.
